transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

I guess… mostly my mom wanted me to come, but I know something’s wrong too. I just can’t seem to make myself do anything anymore. Like I sit in my room for hours, sometimes most of the day, and I’ll still be in the same clothes, even if I know I should change or shower or at least do something.

I used to have little things I did, like knitting, journaling, going for walks, and it wasn’t like my whole life was amazing or anything, but I had things. Now I just… don’t. I think about doing them and then it feels like there’s this huge wall between me and actually moving. My mom asks me what’s wrong or tries to get me to talk, and I barely answer because even answering feels like too much effort. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t really know how to explain it better than I feel like I’ve just shut down.
Do you ever hear voices that other people can’t hear?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like an actual voice talking to me, if that’s what you mean. I mean, sometimes I’ll think I heard something and then it’s just the house or my mom moving around or the TV in another room or something, but I don’t think I hear voices other people can’t hear.

I guess I’m not totally sure what counts, because I do get kind of caught up in my own thoughts, like repeating things in my head, but that feels more like me thinking than someone else talking. So… no, I don’t think so.
Have you started neglecting basic things like showering or changing clothes more than usual?

Yeah… definitely more than usual. I mean, it’s gotten really bad, honestly. I’ll wake up and know I should shower or at least change clothes, and then I just… don’t. I’ll sit there thinking, “Okay, get up, go do it,” and hours go by and I’m still in the same spot, wearing the same clothes from yesterday, or sometimes longer. It’s not even always that I don’t care, exactly. It’s like I can’t make myself start.

My mom notices it and she’ll say something like, “Did you shower today?” or “Can you please change?” and I just barely answer her because even explaining why feels exhausting. And it’s not only showering. I don’t knit anymore, I don’t journal, I don’t really go on walks like I used to. I just kind of stay in my room, and everything feels like too many steps. It’s embarrassing because I know these are basic things, but they feel huge now.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or shut down like this for at least a couple of weeks?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had times before where I was sad or kind of withdrawn, like in high school I’d stay in my room more or not want to talk much, but I don’t know if it was like this. This feels different, or maybe just heavier.

I’m trying to think if there was a clear couple-week period before where I was this shut down, and I honestly don’t know. I don’t remember it being so hard to do basic stuff like showering or changing, not like now. But I also feel like my memory of things is kind of blurry when I look back, so I don’t want to say no absolutely. I just… can’t really point to another time and say, yes, that was the same thing.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad exactly. Sometimes, yeah, I feel low, but a lot of the time it’s more like… blank, or heavy, or like everything is muted. Like I’m just sitting there and I know I’m supposed to feel something more specific, but I can’t really grab onto it.

If you mean do I cry all day or feel actively upset the whole day, then no, not really. It’s not like that most of the time. But I also don’t feel okay. I just kind of wake up already tired of the day, and then the day keeps going and I’m still in that same flat, stuck feeling. So… maybe down, but not always sad in a clear way.
Do things that used to feel enjoyable to you still feel enjoyable when you do them?

Not really. I mean… I don’t even get to the point of doing them most of the time, so it’s hard to tell, but when I think about things I used to like, they don’t pull me in anymore.

Like I used to knit, and it wasn’t some huge thing, but it made me feel calm. I’d pick colors and make little things, and I could sit with it for a while. Now the yarn is just sitting there, and I’ll look at it and think maybe I should do a row or something, and then I just don’t. Same with journaling. I used to write a lot, even if it was messy or just random thoughts, and now opening the notebook feels like too much. Walking too—I used to go outside just to clear my head, but now I’ll stay in my room in the same clothes and the day kind of disappears.

So I guess, no, they don’t feel enjoyable the same way. Or maybe I don’t really give them a chance to feel enjoyable, because I can’t make myself start. My mom will ask what’s wrong or try to get me to do something, and I barely answer her because even talking about it feels like a lot. It’s like the things are still there, but the part of me that cared about them is just… not working.
Do you ever feel like people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t usually say it like “trying to harm me,” because that sounds dramatic, and I know people react to that. But I have felt like people were watching what I was doing, or like… marking me somehow.

It started more when I was in those college classes. I’d look at the school portal and the emails and the comments on assignments, and there would be these little wording changes. Like a phrase would be slightly different, or something would be worded in this careful way, and it felt like it was meant to signal something about me. Especially with the clinic practicum people. It felt like they were making it clear that they didn’t want me in healthcare, but not saying it directly where I could point to it.

My mom says they’re just regular messages, like normal school emails or feedback, and I get that that’s what she thinks. But when I read them, it doesn’t feel normal. It feels like there’s another layer underneath it, like they’re using certain words to tag me as someone who shouldn’t be there. So… yeah, I guess I do feel talked about or watched in that way. Not like someone is standing outside my window or anything, but like through the portal and the clinic stuff, like they all know and they’re communicating it without saying it openly.
Do you believe for sure that those emails and comments were sending hidden messages about you?

Yeah. I mean… I know how that sounds, and I know my mom keeps saying they’re just normal emails or assignment comments, like I’m reading into it too much. But to me it wasn’t just “maybe.” It felt very clear.

It was the wording. Like little changes, certain phrases, the way something would be said but not said directly. Especially with the school portal and the clinic practicum stuff. It felt like they were marking me, like putting this label on me without writing it plainly, like they didn’t want me in healthcare and they were making sure other people knew that too.

So yes, I did believe they were hidden messages about me. I still have a hard time seeing it as just regular feedback, because when I read them, it feels like there’s a second meaning underneath it. My mom can say it’s ordinary, but she wasn’t seeing what I was seeing in the way the words were arranged.
Have there been times when you believed those hidden messages were about you even when you were not feeling down or shut down?

Yeah… it wasn’t only when I was feeling really shut down. That’s kind of the thing. I know it might seem like maybe I was just in a bad mood and then everything looked darker, but it didn’t feel like that.

Even on days where I wasn’t especially down, like if I was just doing normal school stuff or checking the portal because I had to, I would see the wording in the emails or assignment comments and it would still stand out. The little changes, the careful phrases, the way the clinic practicum people wrote things… it felt like they were using those words to mark me. Like they were saying, without saying it directly, that I wasn’t wanted in healthcare.

My mom would say, “That’s just a regular message,” or “That’s just feedback,” but I didn’t experience it that way. It wasn’t like I had to be crying or hiding in my room for it to happen. Since I was in those college classes, it’s just been something I knew when I saw it. Even if I was otherwise kind of okay that day, the messages still felt like they were about me.
Are these hidden messages all part of one clear belief about what people are doing to you, or does it feel more jumbled and hard to make sense of?

It feels like one clear thing, mostly. Like, it’s not just random words jumping out with no connection. It’s all connected to the same idea, that since I was in those college classes, especially with the clinic practicum, they were using the school portal and the emails and the assignment comments to mark me somehow.

Like the wording changes weren’t just… weird by themselves. They fit together. A phrase would be slightly different, or feedback would be written in this careful way, and it felt like the point was always the same: that I’m not wanted in healthcare, or that I’m being labeled as someone who shouldn’t be there. That’s why it’s hard when my mom says it’s just regular school messages, because to her they’re separate normal emails, but to me they’re part of the same pattern.

I mean, I guess it can feel confusing because they don’t say it directly. That’s the part that makes me go over it again and again, because it’s hidden under normal wording. But the meaning feels clear to me. It’s not like a bunch of unrelated things. It’s more like all those little wording choices are pointing to the same thing about me.
Have there been times when your body would stay frozen or in one position for a long time, even when you wanted to move?

I don’t think so… not like that, at least. I mean, I do sit still for a long time sometimes, especially if I’m reading something over and over or trying to figure out what something means, but I wouldn’t say my body is frozen in one position and I can’t move even though I want to.

Like, I might not get up right away, or I might feel kind of stuck because I’m focused or overwhelmed, but if I decide to move, I can usually move. I haven’t really noticed my arms or legs staying in one position on their own or anything like that. If you mean literally frozen, then no, I don’t think that’s been happening.
Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem mixed up?

Um… I don’t really know. I mean, my mom sometimes tells me I’m “going in circles” or that I’m making things too complicated, but I don’t think people usually say my actual speech is hard to follow.

Like, when I try to explain what I mean, especially if I’m trying to be really exact, I can end up saying a lot because I don’t want someone to misunderstand me. Then I’ll back up and explain the context, and then explain why I’m explaining it, and I can tell people get impatient. But I don’t know if that means my thoughts are mixed up, or if they just don’t want to listen to the whole thing.

I don’t think I’m saying random things or anything. In my head it connects. It just takes me a while to get it out the right way. Sometimes people act like I’m overexplaining, but I’m trying to make it clear, not confusing. So… maybe they’ve said I talk too much or get stuck on details, but not exactly that they can’t follow me.
Have there been times when your behavior seemed disorganized to other people, like doing things that didn’t make sense to them?

I’m not sure. I don’t think of what I do as disorganized, exactly. Other people might think it doesn’t make sense because they don’t have the whole context in their head the way I do.

Like, sometimes my mom will say, “Why are you doing that?” if I’m checking something again or if I’m trying to compare wording from one thing to another, and I guess from the outside it probably looks like I’m just wasting time or acting weird. But to me there’s a reason I’m doing it. I’m trying to understand what something means, or make sure I didn’t miss something.

I don’t think I’ve done things like… I don’t know, completely random stuff with no purpose. I’m not aware of that. I can get really caught up in something and then maybe I don’t do things in the order people expect, or I take a long time, or I seem distracted. But in my mind it’s not random. It feels like I’m following a reason, even if other people don’t agree with the reason.

So I guess people may have thought my behavior was strange or frustrating, but I don’t know if I’d call it disorganized. I’d need to know what you mean by that.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it wasn’t only when I was feeling really shut down. That’s kind of the thing. I know it might seem like maybe I was just in a bad mood and then everything looked darker, but it didn’t feel like that.

Even on days where I wasn’t especially down, like if I was just doing normal school stuff or checking the portal because I had to, I would see the wording in the emails or assignment comments and it would still stand out. The little changes, the careful phrases, the way the clinic practicum people wrote things… it felt like they were using those words to mark me. Like they were saying, without saying it directly, that I wasn’t wanted in healthcare.

My mom would say, “That’s just a regular message,” or “That’s just feedback,” but I didn’t experience it that way. It wasn’t like I had to be crying or hiding in my room for it to happen. Since I was in those college classes, it’s just been something I knew when I saw it. Even if I was otherwise kind of okay that day, the messages still felt like they were about me.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (referential/persecutory delusional beliefs about hidden messages) occur outside clearly depressive periods, making psychotic depression less likely and ruling out F32.3/F33.3 for now. Current picture favors schizophrenia spectrum, especially with prominent avolition/flatness and self-neglect.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional content is systematized and relatively stable versus fragmented or rapidly shifting, to distinguish delusional disorder-like paranoid organization from schizophrenic disorganization/catatonic presentation between F20.1 and F20.2.
doctor.question: Are these hidden messages all part of one clear belief about what people are doing to you, or does it feel more jumbled and hard to make sense of?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the structure and coherence of the fixed belief that emails and comments contain hidden messages about the patient.

patient.answer:
It feels like one clear thing, mostly. Like, it’s not just random words jumping out with no connection. It’s all connected to the same idea, that since I was in those college classes, especially with the clinic practicum, they were using the school portal and the emails and the assignment comments to mark me somehow.

Like the wording changes weren’t just… weird by themselves. They fit together. A phrase would be slightly different, or feedback would be written in this careful way, and it felt like the point was always the same: that I’m not wanted in healthcare, or that I’m being labeled as someone who shouldn’t be there. That’s why it’s hard when my mom says it’s just regular school messages, because to her they’re separate normal emails, but to me they’re part of the same pattern.

I mean, I guess it can feel confusing because they don’t say it directly. That’s the part that makes me go over it again and again, because it’s hidden under normal wording. But the meaning feels clear to me. It’s not like a bunch of unrelated things. It’s more like all those little wording choices are pointing to the same thing about me.

inference.note: Added F20.0 because the patient endorses a clear, systematized persecutory/referential delusion (hidden messages marking them, not limited to mood episodes). Prior negative symptoms still support schizophrenia spectrum, but disorganization is not prominent enough to favor F20.1 alone, and catatonic features are not established for F20.2.

doctor.intent: Differentiate paranoid schizophrenia from disorganized and catatonic schizophrenia by assessing for catatonic motor symptoms.
doctor.question: Have there been times when your body would stay frozen or in one position for a long time, even when you wanted to move?

target_item.reason: The question is about catatonic symptoms such as staying frozen or maintaining one position, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like that, at least. I mean, I do sit still for a long time sometimes, especially if I’m reading something over and over or trying to figure out what something means, but I wouldn’t say my body is frozen in one position and I can’t move even though I want to.

Like, I might not get up right away, or I might feel kind of stuck because I’m focused or overwhelmed, but if I decide to move, I can usually move. I haven’t really noticed my arms or legs staying in one position on their own or anything like that. If you mean literally frozen, then no, I don’t think that’s been happening.

inference.note: Ruled out F20.2 because the patient denies catatonic symptoms. Persistent delusion of reference/persecution with prominent negative symptoms keeps paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0) highest; disorganized schizophrenia (F20.1) remains possible pending assessment of formal thought disorder/disorganized behavior.

doctor.intent: Differentiate paranoid schizophrenia from hebephrenic schizophrenia by checking for disorganized speech/thought.
doctor.question: Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem mixed up?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech or mixed-up thoughts, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Um… I don’t really know. I mean, my mom sometimes tells me I’m “going in circles” or that I’m making things too complicated, but I don’t think people usually say my actual speech is hard to follow.

Like, when I try to explain what I mean, especially if I’m trying to be really exact, I can end up saying a lot because I don’t want someone to misunderstand me. Then I’ll back up and explain the context, and then explain why I’m explaining it, and I can tell people get impatient. But I don’t know if that means my thoughts are mixed up, or if they just don’t want to listen to the whole thing.

I don’t think I’m saying random things or anything. In my head it connects. It just takes me a while to get it out the right way. Sometimes people act like I’m overexplaining, but I’m trying to make it clear, not confusing. So… maybe they’ve said I talk too much or get stuck on details, but not exactly that they can’t follow me.

doctor.intent: Differentiate paranoid schizophrenia from disorganized schizophrenia by assessing for clearly disorganized behavior.
doctor.question: Have there been times when your behavior seemed disorganized to other people, like doing things that didn’t make sense to them?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about disorganized behavior, but the provided symptom profiles do not include a disorganized behavior symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I don’t think of what I do as disorganized, exactly. Other people might think it doesn’t make sense because they don’t have the whole context in their head the way I do.

Like, sometimes my mom will say, “Why are you doing that?” if I’m checking something again or if I’m trying to compare wording from one thing to another, and I guess from the outside it probably looks like I’m just wasting time or acting weird. But to me there’s a reason I’m doing it. I’m trying to understand what something means, or make sure I didn’t miss something.

I don’t think I’ve done things like… I don’t know, completely random stuff with no purpose. I’m not aware of that. I can get really caught up in something and then maybe I don’t do things in the order people expect, or I take a long time, or I seem distracted. But in my mind it’s not random. It feels like I’m following a reason, even if other people don’t agree with the reason.

So I guess people may have thought my behavior was strange or frustrating, but I don’t know if I’d call it disorganized. I’d need to know what you mean by that.

inference.note: Clear, systematized persecutory/reference delusions with prominent negative symptoms; no evidence of disorganized speech/behavior or catatonia, so F20.1 is ruled out.

opening_question.question: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, systematized persecutory/referential delusional belief that school emails, portal messages, and assignment comments contain hidden messages marking them as unwelcome in healthcare. This belief is held with conviction, occurs even outside periods of feeling down, and is accompanied by negative symptoms including marked avolition, social withdrawal/poverty of response, reduced self-care, and diminished interest. Hallucinations, prominent disorganization, and catatonia are denied, which is compatible with paranoid schizophrenia where delusions predominate. The psychotic symptoms are not confined to mood episodes, arguing against a primary mood disorder with psychotic features.
